intro: Food groups, cooking methods, flavours and useful language for describing eating patterns.
p.equilibrado.nota: Use equilibrada with a feminine noun, as in una alimentación equilibrada.
p.el marisco.nota: Often refers to shellfish and other seafood, but not finfish.
p.el embutido: cured or processed meats; cold cuts
p.a la plancha.nota: Cooked on a hot flat plate or griddle.
p.frito.nota: Adjective forms agree with the noun: frito, frita, fritos, fritas.
p.hervido.nota: Adjective forms agree with the noun: hervido, hervida, hervidos, hervidas.
p.crudo.nota: Adjective forms agree with the noun: crudo, cruda, crudos, crudas.
p.salado.nota: Describes a salty taste; forms agree with the noun.
p.soso.nota: Of food, bland or lacking flavour; forms agree with the noun.
p.sentar bien.nota: The food is the subject and the person is marked by an indirect-object pronoun: me sienta / me sientan.
p.la dieta mediterránea: the Mediterranean diet; a Mediterranean-style eating pattern
p.la dieta mediterránea.nota: Describes a broad pattern of eating, not one fixed menu.
p.poco hecho.nota: Used especially in Spain for meat doneness; usage varies by region.
p.muy hecho.nota: Used especially in Spain for meat doneness; usage varies by region.
b1.titulo: How it is cooked, how it tastes
b1.texto:
**Cooking and agreement.** The cooking method follows the food name: **pescado a la plancha**. Adjectives agree with the food: **verduras crudas**, **carne poco hecha** or **muy hecha**. **Frito** and **hervido** are also used as food descriptions.

**Taste.** When you describe how a dish tastes now, **estar** is common: **Pruebo el marisco: está soso.** **Ser** can describe a more general characteristic. The choice depends on meaning and context. Other taste words include **salado**, **dulce**, **amargo** and **picante**.

**Sentar bien / mal** works like **gustar**: the food is the subject and the person is marked by a pronoun: **el marisco me sienta mal**; **las legumbres te sientan bien**. The verb agrees with the food.

**Eating patterns.** A Mediterranean-style pattern often includes **fruta**, **verdura**, **legumbres**, **pescado** and **aceite de oliva**. Some descriptions limit **carne roja** and **embutido**, but eating patterns and needs vary.

A balanced, varied diet can take many forms. A general recommendation is that we eat a variety of foods and moderate salt. Nutrition words: **vitaminas**, **proteínas**, **fibra**, **hierro**, **calorías**. For general statements about food groups, Spanish often uses the definite article: **la fruta**, **el aceite de oliva**. Eating slowly and in company are also part of some food traditions.
b2.f0: The Mediterranean diet is often described as a healthy eating pattern, though it is not one fixed menu that suits everyone.
b2.f1: It often includes fruit, vegetables, pulses, fish and olive oil.
b2.f2: Lentils and chickpeas contain protein and fibre.
b2.f3: Some descriptions of the Mediterranean pattern recommend moderating red and processed meats, although practices and needs vary.
b2.f4: The general recommendation is to eat a variety of foods and moderate salt; needs vary from person to person.
b2.f5: But what people eat is not the only thing that matters: some traditions also value eating slowly and with others.
b4.pregunta: You taste the shellfish and comment on how it tastes now. Complete: “It is bland.”
b4.o0.refuerzo: This describes how the dish tastes now.
b4.o1.refuerzo: This would describe a more general characteristic.
b5.pregunta: Complete: shellfish doesn't agree with me.
b5.o1.refuerzo: Siente is from sentir, to feel.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Crudo means raw, not cooked; frito and hervido both describe cooked food.
b7.pregunta: According to the text, what do lentils and chickpeas have?
b7.o1.refuerzo: A lot of fat is a distractor; the question asks about protein and fibre.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Salt is a distractor; the question asks what the pulses have, not salt.
b8.pregunta: Complete: the general recommendation is that we eat a variety of foods.
b8.o0.refuerzo: The construction «la recomendación es que» takes the subjunctive.
b8.o2.refuerzo: The clause needs a conjugated verb.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about your diet: what you eat, what you should eat more or less of, and why.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Give your opinion aloud on fast food, vegetarian diets or eating at set times.
